messages:
Alice Kim: Hey team — filing this thread because 3 customers hit 429s + high p95 latencies during the internal mid-day load test at ~11:12 PT. They reported API errors and timeouts, and support got billing noise too (spikes in request counts). Repro notes attached below.

infra-bot: [alert] 2026-06-02T18:12:45Z: Surge detected on prod-us-west: RPS spike 4.8x baseline, 5 consecutive 5xx rate-limited responses from gateway.

Alice Kim: Quick summary of what customers saw: 1) 429s with body: "rate limit exceeded" 2) 503 timeouts during retries 3) inflated billing-meter logs (we saw duplicate retries incrementing counters).

Alice Kim: Repro steps we used to confirm locally:
```
# k6-ish pseudo script used by QE
scenarios: {
  burst_load: {
    executor: "constant-vus",
    vus: 400,
    duration: "3m",
    exec: "call_api"
  }
}
function call_api() {
  http.post(apiUrl, payload, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TEST_KEY}` }})
}
```
We ran a few variants: 400 VUs / 3m, 800 VUs / 1m, and a 1m ramp to 2k RPS. The 429s only showed up when we pushed sustained RPM/TPM above ~1200rpm and also during sudden step increases (>3x in 10s).

Ben Ortiz: Thanks Alice. I dug into rate-limiter logs. We saw token-bucket refills exhausted for several customer rate-classes. The gateway returned 429 with x-rate-limit headers showing remaining=0 and reset window ~30s. Also saw umask where retries from clients created short burst feedback loops; some clients retried quickly (100–200ms) and got queued spikes.

Ben Ortiz: Key logs (sanitized):
```
[18:12:50Z] gateway rate_limiter: user_id=acct_42 class=standard bucket_tokens=0 refill_period=60s window=60s allowed=0
[18:12:51Z] proxy: upstream_timeout code=504 route=/v1/generate user=acct_42
```

Carol Nguyen: Runtime notes — our current burst config for hosted tier (standard) is: base RPM=600, burst_capacity=2x (allow short bursts up to 1200rpm for 10s), token bucket refill window=60s, per-key concurrency cap=10. The internal test exceeded 2x and held longer than 10s so buckets stayed depleted. Also the gateway enforces per-IP and per-key limits; when traffic came from shared infra IPs during the load test, per-IP quotas triggered earlier than per-key.

Carol Nguyen: Two explanatory diagrams: (lol, ascii)
```
Token bucket: [||||||||||] --requests--> [deplete]-> [refill wait]
Short bursts (t < burst_window) are ok; sustained t > burst_window => steady-state governed by base RPM.
```

Tina Lopez: For support messaging, customers want: 1) what happened 2) whether they're billed for failed requests 3) mitigation steps we took. @billing-bot any quick note about charge behavior when requests are 429/504?

billing-bot: 429 responses are not billed for generated tokens; inbound request count increments for rate metrics but token-usage billing only counts successfully processed tokens. 504 upstream timeouts may result in partial billing if tokens were emitted before timeout; we need request-level tracing to confirm.

Ben Ortiz: Actionable items I propose:
- Short-term: increase burst_window from 10s -> 20s for standard tier and increase burst_capacity to 3x for controlled internal experiments. Also add immediate guard to drop automated internal load test traffic into a separate routing class so it doesn't share per-IP limits with customer traffic.
- Mid-term: implement adaptive backoff guidance: detect client retry storms and return Retry-After header + jitter recommendation.
- Long-term: revisit default RPM to 800 and TPM defaults based on real customer profiles (we should run portfolio-weighted benchmarks).

Carol Nguyen: I ran a focused benchmark on a staging replica with the proposed configs. Commands: 
```
# one-liner used
hey --qps 1200 --concurrency 250 -n 180000 https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Results (staging, 2x A100 equiv):
- baseline config: p50=120ms p95=900ms 429s when >35s sustained at 1200rpm
- proposed config (burst_window=20s burst_capacity=3x): p50=130ms p95=420ms 429s only when >90s sustained at 2.5x baseline

Carol Nguyen: TL;DR — bumping burst window/capacity buys us headroom for our internal tests and accidental step-ups without catastrophic 429s, but it increases tail latency slightly and makes true throttling slower to react. We should only enable higher burst for internal test routing or opt-in customers.

Dave Patel: From product/SLA POV, we can't silently raise bursts for all customers — that changes the shape of fairness and could increase noisy-neighbor exposures. I'm +1 to special routing for internal tests and an opt-in 'burst-friendly' flag for customers who accept higher transient latencies. Also want a runbook update before we tell customers anything.

Alice Kim: Reply template draft for customers hit by the spike: 
"Hey — we ran an internal load test that overlapped with your traffic and caused rate-limit hits for some requests. We have disabled the test, adjusted our internal test routing, and are increasing our test burst windows. Your successful requests and token billing are unaffected; failed 429s were not billed. We’ll follow up with a root-cause report by EOD"

Tina Lopez: I'll send that template and CC folks. Also can we add a short blurb in status.redwood.ai about internal testing windows? Customers asked for transparency.

Ben Ortiz: Next steps I'm going to take tonight: 1) patch routing to mark internal test cluster IPs to 'internal-test' class (no per-IP mixing) 2) deploy config bump to staging 3) run portfolio-weighted benchmark to find sane RPM/TPM defaults and post results here.

Carol Nguyen: I'll coordinate the staging runs and share k6/hey scripts + the exact machine profile and seq length distribution. We should include cold-start & KV-cache-warm cases.

Alice Kim: Thanks — please @me when you have the run outputs. I'll hold off customer emails until we confirm numbers. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [deploy] 2026-06-02T20:04:03Z: Config patch 'internal-test-routing' deployed to staging (carol.nguyen).

Carol Nguyen: Pushed the first benchmark summary to the shared folder: s3://redwood-internal/loadtests/2026-06-02/burst-experiment-1.csv (private). High-level numbers: weighted p95 across customer profiles moved from 780ms->450ms with internal-test routing + burst-window bump.

Dave Patel: Once Ben confirms no customer-impact on prod, we should add a short note on the Console 'rate limits' doc about 'internal test' routing and how we isolate it.

Ben Ortiz: Will do a prod dry-run on the routing change tomorrow during maintenance window and monitor 1h after. If anything odd, I'll rollback.

Alice Kim: Great. Closing loop: I'll draft the customer postmortem + template and share for review. If someone wants to add technical details for the postmortem, drop them here.
